items.followUp: Why does an energy saver use less electricity than an incandescent lamp to produce the same amount of light?

rubric.why: This states the key comparison between the light produced and the power used.
rubric.description: States that an energy saver produces the same amount of light while using less electrical power.
rubric.how: Award for both the same light output and lower power use.

rubric.why: This explains that less energy is wasted as heat.
rubric.description: States that an energy saver is more efficient or wastes less energy as heat.
rubric.how: Award for identifying greater efficiency or reduced heat waste.

modelAnswer: An energy saver produces the same amount of light as an ordinary electric lamp while using less electrical power.
It is more efficient and wastes less energy as heat.

items.followUp: What does the prefix milli mean? Give one unit that uses it.

rubric.why: Prefixes are written before units and indicate multiples or submultiples.
rubric.description: Defines prefixes in relation to units.
rubric.how: Award for stating that prefixes are written before units and show multiples or submultiples.

rubric.why: Kilo, centi and milli are valid examples of prefixes.
rubric.description: Gives two correct examples of prefixes.
rubric.how: Award for any two correct prefixes.

modelAnswer: Prefixes are symbols or words written before units to show multiples or submultiples of those units.
Two examples are kilo (k) and milli (m).
